episodes.title: Introduction to Astronomy
episodes.description: Phil Plait introduces astronomy and the kinds of questions it investigates.

episodes.title: Naked Eye Observations
episodes.description: Discover celestial sights that can be observed outdoors without a telescope.

episodes.title: Cycles in the Sky
episodes.description: Explore repeating patterns visible in the sky and the phenomena behind them.

episodes.title: Moon Phases
episodes.description: Learn why the Moon changes appearance and how its phases are named.

episodes.title: Eclipses
episodes.description: Phil Plait explains eclipses and their place in observing the sky.

episodes.title: Telescopes
episodes.description: Explore telescope operation and considerations when choosing astronomical equipment.

episodes.title: The Gravity of the Situation
episodes.description: Investigate gravity's effects throughout the universe.

episodes.title: Tides
episodes.description: Connect gravitational tides with the locking of planets and moons.

episodes.title: Introduction to the Solar System
episodes.description: Trace the solar system's transformation from a gas cloud into planets and other bodies.

episodes.title: The Sun
episodes.description: Explore the Sun's interior, magnetic activity, eruptions, and effects on Earth.

episodes.title: The Earth
episodes.description: Begin a tour of the solar system's planets with Earth itself.

episodes.title: The Moon
episodes.description: Tour the Moon's surface and interior while exploring ideas about its origin.

episodes.title: Mercury
episodes.description: Explore Mercury's cratered surface, extreme conditions, and hidden ice deposits.

episodes.title: Venus
episodes.description: Investigate Venus's intense heat, greenhouse effect, and volcanic activity.

episodes.title: Mars
episodes.description: Examine Mars's landscape and interior while considering its history and possible future exploration.

episodes.title: Jupiter
episodes.description: Explore Jupiter's atmosphere, long-lived storm, internal heat, and unusual deep interior.

episodes.title: Jupiter’s Moons
episodes.description: Compare Jupiter's major moons and the distinct worlds they represent.

episodes.title: Saturn
episodes.description: Explore Saturn's icy rings, gravitational gaps, and remarkable moons.

episodes.title: Uranus & Neptune
episodes.description: Compare the interiors, atmospheres, rotation, rings, and moons of the two ice giants.

episodes.title: Asteroids
episodes.description: Investigate asteroid locations, composition, and origins.

episodes.title: Comets
episodes.description: Explore how icy bodies release gas and dust as they approach the Sun.

episodes.title: The Oort Cloud
episodes.description: Travel beyond Neptune to the reservoirs of icy objects that can supply comets.

episodes.title: Meteors
episodes.description: Distinguish meteoroids, meteors, and meteorites while exploring showers and impacts.

episodes.title: Light
episodes.description: Use light's wavelengths and spectra to learn about distant objects' physical properties.

episodes.title: Distances
episodes.description: Trace methods astronomers developed to measure distances across space.

episodes.title: Stars
episodes.description: Classify stars using spectra, temperature, luminosity, and the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram.

episodes.title: Exoplanets
episodes.description: Explore methods for finding planets around other stars, including transits and stellar motion.

episodes.title: Brown Dwarfs
episodes.description: Explore brown dwarfs and how their masses compare with giant planets and small stars.

episodes.title: Low Mass Stars
episodes.description: Follow how lower-mass stars consume fuel and change as they age.

episodes.title: White Dwarfs & Planetary Nebulae
episodes.description: Explore the dense remnants and glowing gas clouds left by dying lower-mass stars.

episodes.title: High Mass Stars
episodes.description: Trace heavy-element formation and explosive collapse in massive stars.

episodes.title: Neutron Stars
episodes.description: Investigate dense stellar remnants, pulsars, and the powerful magnetic fields of magnetars.

episodes.title: Black Holes
episodes.description: Explore black-hole formation, possible endings, and extreme tidal stretching.

episodes.title: Binary and Multiple Stars
episodes.description: Learn how connected star systems form, remain bound, interact, and sometimes explode.

episodes.title: Star Clusters
episodes.description: Compare collections of stars held together by gravity and how those collections evolve.

episodes.title: Nebulae
episodes.description: Explore clouds of gas and dust, their colors, and the different ways they become visible.

episodes.title: The Milky Way
episodes.description: Tour the Milky Way's disk, spiral structure, central region, and star-forming environments.

episodes.title: Galaxies, Part 1
episodes.description: Compare galaxy shapes and explore how collisions can drive their growth.

episodes.title: Galaxies, Part 2
episodes.description: Explore active galactic centers and how galaxies gather into groups, clusters, and larger structures.

episodes.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts
episodes.description: Trace the discovery of gamma-ray bursts and investigate their different stellar origins.

episodes.title: Dark Matter
episodes.description: Examine indirect evidence for unseen matter through its gravitational effects on cosmic structures.

episodes.title: The Big Bang, Cosmology Part 1
episodes.description: Use galactic redshifts and expansion to reconstruct the universe's beginning.

episodes.title: Dark Energy & Cosmology, Part 2
episodes.description: Explore the mysterious influence accelerating cosmic expansion and its implications for the future.

episodes.title: A Brief History of the Universe
episodes.description: Reconstruct the universe's earliest minutes using physical evidence and theory.

episodes.title: Deep Time
episodes.description: Explore possible far-future outcomes for stars, matter, and black holes over immense cosmic timescales.

episodes.title: Everything, The Universe…And Life
episodes.description: Revisit astronomy's major questions and the possibilities they open for understanding life and the universe.
